Salt air and coastal building maintenance.

We map exposure, material condition and access before separating coastal cleaning, local repairs and replacement work.

Read the exposure before choosing a repair.

Coastal maintenance starts with a location-specific record. A sheltered door, an exposed fixing and a rain-washed wall do not present the same conditions. We document the installed material, visible change and surrounding detail, then build a scope that distinguishes deposits, deterioration and operating faults.

Record the exposure at each location

We look at the face of the building, overhangs, sheltered ledges, door tops and accessible fixings. Photographs show the item and the area around it, allowing later observations to be compared with the same location. The record also identifies the material or product where it is known.

COLORBOND maintenance guidance distinguishes rain-washed surfaces from areas that rain does not wash effectively, and addresses marine salt exposure. We apply the instructions for the installed product. Other metals, coatings, glass and hardware need their own care requirements checked.

Compare rain-washed and sheltered surfaces. Clean deposits on intact coatings with a compatible method. Separately inspect bubbling, exposed metal and recurrent fixing damage.

Roofing & waterproofing ↗
02

Cleaning, repair and replacement have different jobs

Compare a rain-washed surface with a sheltered fixing on the same elevation. A surface deposit, a failing finish and a stiff opening tell us different things. Keeping separate observations makes it easier to agree cleaning, a local repair or a closer inspection.

At two sides of the same building, an exposed panel may be rain-washed while a recessed entrance holds deposits. Once the product and finish are identified, sound surfaces can go on the cleaning list. Repeated coating lift around a joint or movement at a fixing needs a closer inspection of the substrate. We compare a local repair with phased renewal when several adjacent parts share the same deterioration or the original fixings are no longer available.

  • Clean the suitable surface

    We agree the surface, product-compatible method, access and protection. Cleaning can reveal the condition more clearly; it does not restore a failed coating or a damaged component by itself.

  • Repair the defined detail

    A local repair needs an identified defect, sound surrounding material and a workable finish detail. We record the area to be prepared and any matching limitation.

  • Replace where the scope requires it

    Replacement is considered against the component condition, compatibility and intended operation. Adjacent fixings, interfaces and finishes are included when they affect the result.

Read the surface and the moving parts separately.

Separate what is visible

ObservationWhat we checkScope direction
Deposits or surface dirtMaterial, finish and a suitable cleaning methodDefined cleaning area and protection
Coating damage or visible deteriorationExtent, adjacent details and condition beneath the finishRepair investigation and finish treatment
Loose or poorly operating hardwareThe door or window, frame, alignment and related partsAdjustment, part repair or replacement as confirmed
Roofing & waterproofing ↗

Check the complete door or window

Compare a sheltered door fitting with a nearby exposed surface. If the fitting is stiff and the finish only shows deposits, record both separately before deciding whether cleaning, adjustment or closer inspection is appropriate.

Inspect alignment, hinges, frame, latch and moving parts as an assembly before defining a repair.

Existing model details and photographs help us check replacement compatibility. We keep part selection, surface treatment and any broader door or frame work separate in the quotation.

Include access and surrounding areas

  • Occupied spaces

    We identify guest or customer routes, neighbouring glazing, landscaped areas and any equipment needed to reach the work.

  • Cleaning water

    Wash-water handling is part of the method. Gold Coast pollution guidance addresses cleaning runoff; we identify the site arrangements before washing begins.

  • Connected repairs

    Roof, façade, door and external-area items can be grouped for access while retaining separate materials and completion checks.

Build the next visit from the record

We use product instructions, the observed condition and actual exposure to define the next maintenance scope. The same fixed interval is not applied to every component. A location record makes it easier to see whether the deposit or deterioration has changed.

Keep cleaned areas, repairs, replacement parts and follow-up visits together with photographs and material records.

We set review points by product guidance, shelter, use and condition. Frequently used doors and sheltered steel need their own review points, alongside any post-storm walk-through. The work record separates surfaces cleaned, hardware adjusted or renewed, and areas to revisit so routine care can be priced independently of repairs.

Building & general maintenance ↗

Turn observations into a brief.

Send one wide photograph per elevation and close-ups of joints or fixings. Include the material or coating if known and which areas are usually sheltered from rain.

  • Exposure and location notes
  • Surface and fixing photographs
  • Cleaning, repair or review items

Common questions

Common questions

Does a coastal property need one maintenance interval for everything?+

Set site-specific cleaning and review schedules for sheltered metal, moving hardware and drainage points.

Should a stained metal surface be repainted immediately?+

We first identify the material and visible condition. Deposits, coating failure and underlying deterioration require different preparation and treatment, so the repainting extent follows that assessment.
